gaps.sentence: He ___ very shy at first, but once you know him he is very chatty.
gaps.hint: seem describes a state not action
gaps.explanation: 'Seem' describes a state and is not used continuously: seems.

gaps.sentence: When I got home, I realised I ___ my keys at the office.
gaps.explanation: 'Had left' — the leaving happened before the realising.

gaps.sentence: I ___ to contact him all week, but his phone is always engaged.
gaps.hint: all week repeated attempts until now
gaps.explanation: Repeated attempts continuing up to now take the present perfect continuous: have been trying.

gaps.sentence: This time next week I ___ on a beach in Portugal, with my phone switched off.
gaps.hint: this time next week means in progress
gaps.explanation: 'This time next week' points to an action in progress at a future moment, so the future continuous fits: will be lying.

gaps.sentence: No sooner ___ the match kicked off than it started pouring.
gaps.explanation: 'No sooner had … than …' — past perfect with inversion.

gaps.sentence: This is the best pizza I ___ in years.
gaps.hint: superlative experience counted up to now
gaps.explanation: Superlative statements about experience up to now take the present perfect: have eaten.

gaps.sentence: Who ___ this bag belong to? It has been sitting here all morning.
gaps.hint: the question form needs auxiliary does
gaps.explanation: Present simple questions need the auxiliary 'does' plus the base verb: does this bag belong to.

gaps.sentence: While we ___ through the forest, we saw a family of deer.
gaps.explanation: 'While' introduces the longer background action, which takes the past continuous: were hiking.
